metadata.title: Chip stocks tumble as Nvidia-led AI rally unravels, tariff fears weigh

content.text:
Global chip stocks tumbled on Wednesday, with Nvidia and memory makers leading a broad retreat in technology shares as concerns over artificial intelligence valuations, US tariffs and interest rates weighed on investor sentiment.
Nvidia Corp (NASDAQ:NVDA, XETRA:NVD) fell nearly 9%, reversing much of Monday's rally following comments and developments involving CEO Jensen Huang.
Chip designer Arm Holdings PLC (NASDAQ:ARM) dropped 8%, while Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co (ADR) (NYSE:TSM), which manufactures Nvidia's chips, and semiconductor equipment maker ASML Holding NV (NASDAQ:ASML, XETRA:ASME) each lost more than 3%.
Memory chipmakers Micron Technology Inc (NASDAQ:MU) and South Korea's SK Hynix fell roughly 10%, giving back some of Monday's double-digit gains. Storage companies Sandisk, Seagate Technology and Western Digital also declined.
The Nasdaq fell more than 4% at one stage, while the S&P 500 was down around 2.5%, as investors reassessed the outlook for technology and AI-related companies.
"Investors are back to dumping tech stocks with indecent haste, but now everything else is being dragged into it too," said Chris Beauchamp, chief market analyst at IG.
He said Monday's rally, which followed Huang's return to the spotlight, had provided markets with only a brief reprieve, adding that US investors were focused on getting through the Thanksgiving holiday without further losses.
Kathleen Brooks, research director at XTB, said concerns about AI valuations were combining with tariff uncertainty and expectations for interest rates to intensify the sell-off.
Brooks said questions around Nvidia's corporate governance, potential circular financing arrangements and exposure to Chinese revenue channels were also weighing on sentiment.
The stronger growth and persistent inflation could reinforce expectations that US interest rates will remain elevated, increasing financing costs for the AI infrastructure build-out.
Brooks noted that Nvidia's credit default swap spreads had approached record levels, although she stressed that the company was unlikely to face default given its substantial cash generation. Nvidia reported more than $40 billion in free cash flow in its latest quarter.
AI company Anthropic (NASDAQ:ANT) also fell 5%, trading below its IPO price, adding to evidence of weakening appetite for the sector.
Brooks said the Nasdaq 100 had returned to levels seen last week, suggesting Monday's rebound may have been a temporary relief rally rather than the start of a sustained recovery.
